sentences.zh: 其中一位是威尔士女仆，她的名字叫玛丽·刘易斯。

sentences.en: And she has had, I think it's fair to say, a pretty awful life back home in Wales, hasn't she?
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，她在威尔士老家的生活相当糟糕，不是吗？

sentences.en: So tell us about her and why she's come over to Pynchon's town.
sentences.zh: 所以告诉我们关于她的事，以及她为什么来到平琼的城镇。

sentences.en: Mary Lewis back in Monmouthshire, she gets married, her husband turns out to be a wrongan, he's a Catholic in what is after all a Protestant country.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·刘易斯在蒙茅斯郡结婚了，结果她的丈夫是个混蛋，在一个毕竟是新教国家的国家里，他是个天主教徒。

sentences.en: That is a wrongan.
sentences.zh: 那确实是个混蛋。

sentences.en: And that is, he is a real, but he's also horrible as well and he abuses her and he deserts her and he, you know, sorry, bullies her, then he deserts her.
sentences.zh: 而且，他不仅是个混蛋，还很可怕，他虐待她，抛弃了她，他，你知道，抱歉，欺负她，然后抛弃了她。

sentences.en: And so, you know, there's this kind of spiritual and emotional void in her life.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，她的生活中有一种精神和情感上的空虚。

sentences.en: She just feels, as I think many, you know, potential migrants do, that there's nothing left for her there.
sentences.zh: 她只是觉得，我想许多潜在的移民都有同感，她在那里已经一无所有了。

sentences.en: And she joins this rather kind of charismatic, you know, radical Protestant community in Wales.
sentences.zh: 她加入了威尔士一个相当有魅力的激进新教社区。

sentences.en: So she's already kind of being set up for the kind of world that she might go to in New England.
sentences.zh: 所以她已经在为她可能去往的新英格兰世界做准备了。

sentences.en: Of course, others are going too.
sentences.zh: 当然，其他人也在去。

sentences.en: And so the time comes that it's, you know, she can get on a boat and go and completely start over.
sentences.zh: 所以时机到了，你知道，她可以上船去，彻底重新开始。

sentences.en: And so Malcolm, in this sect, and presumably going to America, she is very, very conscious
sentences.zh: 那么马尔科姆，在这个教派中，想必去往美国，她非常、非常清楚

sentences.en: of this division between those who are saved and those who aren't, between those who have won the light and those who were threatened with perdition.
sentences.zh: 得救者与未得救者之间的这种划分，在那些赢得了光明的人与那些受到永罚威胁的人之间。

sentences.en: Yeah, she is.
sentences.zh: 是的，她是。

sentences.en: I think that like many, she probably doesn't expect that she's going to have to prove herself because of course, those who, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想像许多人一样，她可能没想到自己必须证明自己，因为当然，那些，你知道，

sentences.en: in England and in Wales who believe themselves to be part of the elect, they're very sure of themselves in that regard.
sentences.zh: 在英国和威尔士那些认为自己是选民一部分的人，他们在这一点上非常自信。

sentences.en: And so, you know, she's going to be tested in a totally new way.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，她将以一种全新的方式受到考验。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone is tested materially and spiritually.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每个人都在物质和精神上受到考验。

sentences.en: That's one of the things that makes this experience so tough.
sentences.zh: 这就是让这种经历变得如此艰难的原因之一。

sentences.en: So she, she doesn't, she sort of knows what she's, you know, she's in for, but I don't think anybody is quite prepared for the challenges that that makes on them personally.
sentences.zh: 所以她，她并没有，她有点知道她，你知道，她要面对什么，但我认为没有人完全准备好迎接这对他们个人造成的挑战。

sentences.en: And how does she end up in
sentences.zh: 那么她最终是如何来到

sentences.en: Springfield specifically?
sentences.zh: 斯普林菲尔德的呢？

sentences.en: Is she planning to go there from the beginning or does she just get to do it and then look around?
sentences.zh: 她是计划从一开始就去那里，还是只是到了那里然后四处看看？

sentences.en: No, she gets hired as a May servant and through the kind of Bush telegraph of who needs labour and so on, that William Pynchon hires her to be a maid servant
sentences.zh: 不，她被雇为女仆，通过谁需要劳动力的那种“丛林电报”之类的消息，威廉·平琼雇佣她去给他女儿做女仆，

sentences.en: to his daughter, who has got young children and is pregnant again, and is just going to need help around the house.
sentences.zh: 他女儿有年幼的孩子，又怀孕了，正需要家务方面的帮助。

sentences.en: And that's really how she ends up making that hundred mile journey from the Eastern Seaboard of Massachusetts over to the Connecticut Valley where Springfield is.
sentences.zh: 这就是她最终完成从马萨诸塞东海岸到斯普林菲尔德所在的康涅狄格河谷那一百英里旅程的原因。

sentences.en: And then for someone like Mary, just to sort of paint the picture, when she gets to Springfield,
sentences.zh: 那么对于像玛丽这样的人，为了描绘一下画面，当她到达斯普林菲尔德时，

sentences.en: does she sort of think, Oh, this is, I mean, obviously we don't know what she thinks, but does she, does she sort of think this is just like home?
sentences.zh: 她会想，哦，这是，我的意思是，显然我们不知道她在想什么，但她会想这就像家一样吗？

sentences.en: You know, this is a recreation of home or is it obviously a more anxious, difficult, darker kind of place?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是对家的重建，还是它显然是一个更焦虑、更困难、更黑暗的地方？

sentences.en: Would you say?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么说？

sentences.en: I think it's a mixture.
sentences.zh: 我认为是混合的。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, everyone's trying to seek out the familiar, to recreate the familiar, because of course that's what we do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，每个人都在试图寻找熟悉的事物，重建熟悉的事物，因为当然这就是我们所做的。

sentences.en: You know, that's what, that's what's comforting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是，这就是令人安慰的。

sentences.en: That's the world that you know, but it's just, that is just hard work.
sentences.zh: 那是你所知的世界，但它只是，那只是艰苦的工作。

sentences.en: And the, because they're very conscious of the fact that there are wolves, there are no wolves at home.
sentences.zh: 而且，因为他们非常清楚那里有狼，家里没有狼。

sentences.en: There are Native Americans, no Native Americans at home that, you know, there's hostility with them.
sentences.zh: 有美洲原住民，家里没有美洲原住民，你知道，他们之间存在敌意。

sentences.en: There are shortages of things.
sentences.zh: 物资短缺。

sentences.en: There's epidemic disease.
sentences.zh: 有流行病。

sentences.en: And just this, you know, this wilderness beyond, as they see it, they just don't really know what lies out there.
sentences.zh: 还有这，你知道，他们眼中的荒野，他们真的不知道外面有什么。

sentences.en: And I think everybody feels this existential threat.
sentences.zh: 我认为每个人都感受到了这种生存威胁。

sentences.en: So that England, of course, has its problems in the 1640s and 50s, but nobody ever believes that England will cease to exiSt. They don't know where it's
sentences.zh: 所以英国，当然，在17世纪40和50年代也有它的问题，但没有人会相信英国会停止存在。他们不知道它在哪里

sentences.en: going, but it won't be wiped off the map.
sentences.zh: 会继续存在，但不会从地图上消失。

sentences.en: But that's how they feel about New England.
sentences.zh: 但他们对新英格兰的看法就是这样。

sentences.en: They know that actually in the end, this experiment could fail and they'll all either have to go home or they'll die.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，归根结底，这场实验可能会失败，他们要么得回家，要么就会死。

sentences.en: And for Mary specifically, there's the fact that she is, you know, she's married.
sentences.zh: 对玛丽个人而言，还有一个事实，那就是，你知道的，她已经结婚了。

sentences.en: She's left her abusive husband in England.
sentences.zh: 她抛下了在英国虐待她的丈夫。

sentences.en: She's now working as a maidservant surrounded by children.
sentences.zh: 她现在以女仆的身份工作，身边围绕着孩子。

sentences.en: And she's merely an appendage of the family, you know, of the mistress for whom she's working.
sentences.zh: 她仅仅是这个家庭的附庸，你知道的，是她所服务的女主人的附庸。

sentences.en: But presumably she wants a family as well.
sentences.zh: 但想必她也想要一个家庭。

sentences.en: She wants her independence.
sentences.zh: 她想要独立。

sentences.en: And this is terrible that if you're a spinster, you are mocked as a thorn back.
sentences.zh: 如果一个女人成了老处女，就会被嘲笑为“荆棘背”，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: She doesn't want to be a thorn back.
sentences.zh: 她不想成为“荆棘背”。

sentences.en: She's looking for a potential husband.
sentences.zh: 她在寻找潜在的丈夫。

sentences.en: No, she, I mean, like almost everybody else, she wants to conform.
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，就像几乎其他人一样，她想要随大流。

sentences.en: And in this world, conformity means getting married and having children, having your own separate household.
sentences.zh: 在这个世界上，随大流意味着结婚生子，拥有自己独立的家庭。

sentences.en: This is true for men and women.
sentences.zh: 这对男人和女人都适用。

sentences.en: All young people want to form their own household.
sentences.zh: 所有年轻人都想组建自己的家庭。

sentences.en: That's the, that's why it's so hard in England because you need land and you need work.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在英国那么困难，因为你需要土地，也需要工作。

sentences.en: So they're often going to America not to seek their fortunes.
sentences.zh: 所以他们去美国往往不是为了发财。

sentences.en: I think that's a very kind of modern way of looking at it, but they do want to form a separate family and their own little political as well as economic unit because that's
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种非常现代的看法，但他们确实想要组建一个独立的家庭，建立属于他们自己的小型政治和经济单位，因为这就是

sentences.en: what in the early modern world, that's what the household is.
sentences.zh: 在近代早期世界中，家庭的定义。

sentences.en: So yeah, she wants to basically erase her paSt. She wants to forget her husband.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，她基本上想抹去她的过去。她想忘记她的丈夫。

sentences.en: She wants the marriage to be annulled and she wants to find a new husband and just, just, I think just be normal in that world.
sentences.zh: 她想让婚姻作废，想找个新丈夫，我想，只是想在这个世界上过正常人的生活。

sentences.en: And then as luck would have it, her eye falls on the perfect person.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，她的目光落在了完美的人选身上。

sentences.en: So he is Hugh Parsons.
sentences.zh: 他就是休·帕森斯。

sentences.en: He's a guy that's been brought in to make bricks.
sentences.zh: 他是一个被请来做砖块的人。

sentences.en: They need bricks.
sentences.zh: 他们需要砖块。

sentences.en: They can't buy them.
sentences.zh: 他们买不到。

sentences.en: And she thinks he's a very fine fellow.
sentences.zh: 她觉得他是个非常不错的人。

sentences.en: He's a sort of physically to make, making bricks is hard work.
sentences.zh: 他身体上……做砖块可是苦力活。

sentences.en: He's a physically impressive bloke.
sentences.zh: 他是个身体强壮的家伙。

sentences.en: He's perhaps a little bit quiet as we'll discover.
sentences.zh: 正如我们稍后会发现的，他可能有点沉默寡言。

sentences.en: But so her gaze falls on him.
sentences.zh: 但她的目光确实落在了他身上。

sentences.en: And what's his story?
sentences.zh: 那他的故事是什么呢？

sentences.en: We don't know so much about him, do we?
sentences.zh: 我们对他了解不多，对吧？

sentences.en: He's a bit more...
sentences.zh: 他有点……

sentences.en: No, we know much, much less about him.
sentences.zh: 不，我们对他了解得少之又少。

sentences.en: Not even entirely sure where he comes from.
sentences.zh: 甚至不完全确定他来自哪里。

sentences.en: There are about
sentences.zh: 大约有

sentences.en: 20 or so Hugh Parsons amazingly in England at this time.
sentences.zh: 20个左右的休·帕森斯，令人惊讶的是，当时在英国有这么多同名的人。

sentences.en: So it's, it's a bit hard to tell, but he is, yeah, certainly he must be, I mean, he comes across as a kind of, you know, tall, dark, mysterious man.
sentences.zh: 所以，这有点难说，但他确实，是的，他肯定，我的意思是，他给人的印象是一个，你知道的，高大、深沉、神秘的男人。

sentences.en: I think that maybe, again, it's a speculation, but
sentences.zh: 我想这也许，再次重申，这只是猜测，但

sentences.en: Mary is possibly slightly intrigued by him because he is actually very quiet.
sentences.zh: 玛丽可能对他有点好奇，因为他实际上非常安静。

sentences.en: And this is, this is a characteristic that runs right through everything we know about him.
sentences.zh: 这是贯穿我们所知关于他的一切的一个特征。

sentences.en: He's a, he's a man of few words and also few emotions.
sentences.zh: 他是个话不多，情感也不多的人。

sentences.en: And of course that will cause him problems in due course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这在适当的时候会给他带来麻烦。

sentences.en: But yeah, you know, she likes him, he likes her.
sentences.zh: 但确实，你知道的，她喜欢他，他也喜欢她。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think that it's, it's not a match made in heaven.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我认为这并不是天作之合。

sentences.en: I'm not quite sure where it's made, but they're going to get together.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这算什么，但他们确实要在一起了。

sentences.en: So she gets her marriage annulled, doesn't she?
sentences.zh: 所以她让她的婚姻作废了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She goes to Pynchon and she gets permission because her husband has deserted her.
sentences.zh: 她去找了平琼，并获得了许可，因为她的丈夫抛弃了她。

sentences.en: A Catholic husband back in Wales has deserted her.
sentences.zh: 一个远在威尔士的天主教徒丈夫抛弃了她。

sentences.en: So she and Hugh get married.
sentences.zh: 所以她和休结婚了。

sentences.en: And at first it all looks lovely and rosy.
sentences.zh: 起初一切看起来都很美好、很乐观。

sentences.en: They're starting this new life in together, this new household in Springfield.
sentences.zh: 他们在斯普林菲尔德开始了新的生活，组建了新的家庭。

sentences.en: And maybe we should take a break now because I don't want to, you know, get too deep into spoilers for our listeners.
sentences.zh: 也许我们现在应该休息一下，因为我不想，你知道的，给我们的听众剧透太多。

sentences.en: This story is going to take quite a dark turn, Tom, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这个故事将会变得相当黑暗，汤姆，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It doesn't end well.
sentences.zh: 结局并不好。

sentences.en: So to find out what happens, come back after the break.
sentences.zh: 所以想知道发生了什么，休息之后回来继续收听。

sentences.en: Hello, welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎回到《历史的余味》。

sentences.en: We are in mid 17th century New England, specifically in the newly founded town of Springfield, where a young couple, Hugh and Mary Parsons, have set up house.
sentences.zh: 我们现在身处17世纪中叶的新英格兰，具体是在新建立的斯普林菲尔德镇，一对年轻夫妇，休和玛丽·帕森斯，在那里安了家。

sentences.en: Mary has a succession of children.
sentences.zh: 玛丽接连生了几个孩子。

sentences.en: And here to tell us about what happens to that marriage and to the community of Springfield more generally,
sentences.zh: 今天我们请来了马尔科姆·加斯克尔，他那本精彩著作《所有女巫的毁灭》的作者，来为我们讲述那段婚姻以及斯普林菲尔德社区后来发生的事情。

sentences.en: we have Malcolm Gaskell, author of the brilliant book, The Ruin of All Witches.
sentences.zh: 那么马尔科姆，那段婚姻结果如何？

sentences.en: So Malcolm, how does the marriage turn out?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想起初还不错。

sentences.en: Well, it starts off okay, I think.
sentences.zh: 玛丽很快就怀孕了。

sentences.en: Mary is quite quickly becomes pregnant.
sentences.zh: 她在1646年的夏天生下了一个孩子。

sentences.en: She has a baby in the summer of 1646.
sentences.zh: 他们俩都很努力地做着新英格兰家庭里人们该做的事。

sentences.en: And they both work hard doing what people do in New
sentences.zh: 休在外耕作、做砖块、建烟囱，还为威廉·平琼干活，那是每个人都会做的事。

sentences.en: England households.
sentences.zh: 而她在家里照顾孩子、做饭、打扫卫生。

sentences.en: So Hugh is out working on the land and making bricks and building chimneys and also doing jobs for William Pincham, which is what everybody does.
sentences.zh: 我想起初，他们做得很好。

sentences.en: And she's at home looking after the baby and cooking and cleaning and doing that.
sentences.zh: 但当然，像所有婚姻一样，你必须真正用心经营。

sentences.en: It's I think initially, they get it right.
sentences.zh: 而在斯普林菲尔德，你得付出110%的努力去经营。

sentences.en: But of course, like all marriages, you've got to really work at it.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，你可能还是会出错。

sentences.en: And in Springfield, you've got to work at it like, you know, 110%.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And even then, you might not get it right.
sentences.zh: 那么，把巫术的威胁引入这个故事，我的意思是，这在整个社区上空盘旋，就像联邦的所有社区一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 人们意识到巫术的存在，你知道的，他们并不认为这是迷信。

sentences.en: So the threat of witchcraft, to bring that into the story, I mean, that hangs over the community generally, like all communities in the Union.
sentences.zh: 他们知道外面有一个黑暗的世界，精神世界和物质世界之间的界限，你知道的，薄如蝉翼。

sentences.en: Like people are aware that witchcraft exists, you know, they don't see it as superstition.
sentences.zh: 而玛丽对巫术着了迷，不是吗？

sentences.en: They know there's a dark world out there, that the boundaries between the spiritual and the material are, you know, gossamer thin.
sentences.zh: 她对此变得痴迷。

sentences.en: And she is obsessed by witchcraft, isn't she, Mary?
sentences.zh: 是的，这很奇怪。

sentences.en: She becomes obsessed by it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有趣的是，每个人都知道巫术，不幸的事情也时有发生，他们能感觉到魔鬼的存在。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very odd.
sentences.zh: 但人们真正指控他人行巫术是非常罕见的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's interesting that the people, everybody does know about witchcraft and misfortunes happen all the time and they feel the devil.
sentences.zh: 这在英国也是事实。

sentences.en: But it's very unusual for people to actually accuse others of witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 但在那里，你知道的，斯普林菲尔德已经存在了15年或更久，没有任何关于巫术的记录在案的指控。

sentences.en: And it's true actually in
sentences.zh: 但突然在1647年左右，出现了关于巫术的传言，这些传言来自波士顿和康涅狄格河谷上游。

sentences.en: England too.
sentences.zh: 它似乎正在蔓延。

sentences.en: But there, you know, Springfield's been going for 15 years or more and there's no recorded accusations of witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在任何人指责之前，它就已经弥漫在空气中了。

sentences.en: But that suddenly in around 1647, there are rumours of witchcraft which are coming from Boston and up the Connecticut Valley.
sentences.zh: 玛丽奇怪地变得非常专注于这样一个想法：不仅这里有女巫，而且可能还有来自其他社区的女巫。

sentences.en: It just seems to be taking hold.
sentences.zh: 有一个女人从下游的温莎教区搬来，一个叫默西·马什菲尔德的寡妇。

sentences.en: You know, it's just, it's in the air before actually anybody points the finger.
sentences.zh: 玛丽认定了她，正如她所说，把魔鬼带到了这里。

sentences.en: And Mary strangely does become really rather preoccupied by the idea that there are not just witches in, but that maybe there are witches coming from other communities.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，马尔科姆，读你的书时让我印象深刻的一点是，也许因为我妻子是助产士，巫术偏执似乎与分娩和育儿过程有着绝对的关联。

sentences.zh: 玛丽。

sentences.en: And then actually, they go back to being horrible to each other in new and interesting and exciting ways, ending each other's land and all that.
sentences.zh: 然后实际上，他们又开始以各种新奇有趣的方式互相折磨，侵占彼此的土地等等。

sentences.en: So that actually, it doesn't really, this is the thing about witch hunts, that there's sometimes this rather righteous feeling that actually,
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这并没有真正解决问题，这就是猎巫运动的特点，有时会有一种相当正义的感觉，认为实际上，

sentences.en: if we just get rid of those people, everything will be all right.
sentences.zh: 如果我们除掉那些人，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: But it isn't, because actually, the wickedness really resides in their own hearts.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此，因为实际上，邪恶真正存在于他们自己的心中。

sentences.en: And then in the 1670s, this devastating New England wide war with Native Americans, that really does actually nearly spell the end of New England.
sentences.zh: 然后在1670年代，这场毁灭性的、波及整个新英格兰的与美洲原住民的战争，确实差点导致了新英格兰的终结。

sentences.en: The Native forces get within 10 miles of Boston, and they get to Boston, it would be game over.
sentences.zh: 原住民军队推进到了距离波士顿10英里以内，如果他们打到波士顿，一切就完了。

sentences.en: So this existential threat that's been hanging over them all the time really does reach its climax in the 1670s.
sentences.zh: 所以这种一直笼罩在他们头上的生存威胁，在1670年代确实达到了高潮。

sentences.en: Although Springfield recovers, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 虽然斯普林菲尔德恢复了，不是吗？

sentences.en: And becomes, I learned from your book, the birthplace of Dr. Seuss.
sentences.zh: 而且我从你的书中了解到，它还是苏斯博士的出生地。

sentences.en: It is, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: He has his own memorial sculpture park with life-size sort of cat in the hat and all around the place, which is kind of trippy and odd.
sentences.zh: 他有自己的纪念雕塑公园，到处都是真人大小的“戴帽子的猫”，这感觉有点迷幻和奇怪。

sentences.en: But no, it's very famous, famous for all sorts of other things, birthplace of basketball and the Merriam-Webster Dictionary,
sentences.zh: 但不是，它非常有名，以各种其他事情闻名，是篮球和《韦氏词典》的诞生地，

sentences.en: you know, and Rolls-Royces were made there, and Springfield Armoury made guns for, you know, for generations and generations, right up to the Vietnam War.
sentences.zh: 你知道，劳斯莱斯也曾在那制造，斯普林菲尔德兵工厂制造枪支，你知道，一代又一代，一直持续到越南战争。

sentences.en: So it's a really, comes a really thriving town, and then in the 19th century city too,
sentences.zh: 所以它确实变成了一个非常繁荣的城镇，然后在19世纪也成为了城市，

sentences.en: Dickens goes there.
sentences.zh: 狄更斯也去过那里。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, it's a big civic place, and then, which, like so many other American cities, goes into 20th century decline.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，这是一个重要的市政中心，然后，像许多其他美国城市一样，在20世纪走向了衰落。

sentences.en: But Malcolm, another link to cartoons is that, of course, the hometown of the Simpsons is called Springfield.
sentences.zh: 但马尔科姆，另一个与卡通的联系是，当然，《辛普森一家》的家乡也叫斯普林菲尔德。

sentences.en: Springfield serves as a kind of, you know, an image of America in every town.
sentences.zh: 斯普林菲尔德充当了一种，你知道，每个城镇中美国形象的缩影。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the obvious question, I suppose, that's been hanging over this whole episode, is the extent to which what is happening in our Springfield in the 17th century,
sentences.zh: 我想，整个这一集一直悬而未决的一个显而易见的问题是，我们17世纪的斯普林菲尔德所发生的事情，在多大程度上

sentences.en: to what extent are patterns being established that you can trace throughout the entire course of American history, perhaps into the present?
sentences.zh: 在多大程度上确立了可以在整个美国历史进程中，甚至可能延续到今天都能追踪到的模式？

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, I think there are patterns.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为确实存在一些模式。

sentences.en: They're not necessarily uniquely American, though, I think.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为它们不一定是美国独有的。

sentences.en: I mean, they do, one of the things they do achieve in Springfield, like so many other colonial communities, they do recreate old England.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们确实，他们在斯普林菲尔德实现的一件事，就像许多其他殖民社区一样，他们确实重建了旧英国。

sentences.en: They have rather similar patterns of class stratification and manufacture and agriculture and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们有着相当相似的阶级分层、制造业和农业模式等等。

sentences.en: It's often actually really rather similar.
sentences.zh: 实际上往往非常相似。

sentences.en: You know, the similarity in the end is that people want to belong to something, a society and a community, but essentially want to build their own households.
sentences.zh: 你知道，最终的相似之处在于人们想要归属于某个东西，一个社会和一个社区，但本质上是想建立自己的家庭。

sentences.en: And sometimes they do that comfortably, and sometimes they do it in opposition with their neighbours.
sentences.zh: 有时他们做得心安理得，有时他们是在与邻居的对立中完成的。

sentences.en: And that becomes, actually, I think, a very modern story about how we all live.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上成为了一个关于我们如何生活的非常现代的故事。

sentences.en: But I don't think it's necessarily a uniquely American one.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这不一定是美国独有的。

sentences.en: So I know we've spent a lot of time talking about Springfield and what went on in Springfield, but just to broaden it out again at the end, why do people stop having witch crazies?
sentences.zh: 我知道我们花了很多时间谈论斯普林菲尔德以及那里发生的事情，但最后想再拓宽一下，为什么人们停止了巫术狂热？

sentences.en: The seeds of the destruction of the witch hunt are really there from the start, which I think,
sentences.zh: 猎巫运动毁灭的种子其实从一开始就存在了，我认为，

sentences.en: as we talked about earlier, is about the uncertainty of having the kind of proof and being confident
sentences.zh: 正如我们之前谈到的，这是关于拥有那种证据的不确定性，以及对现有证据是否自信的问题，

sentences.en: in the proof that is available, which is essentially witness testimony, which today we would just call hearsay.
sentences.zh: 这本质上就是证人证言，今天我们只会称之为传闻。

sentences.en: And I think that by the early 18th century, this development of this awareness of hearsay of inadmissible evidence in court really just does for witch hunting.
sentences.zh: 我认为到18世纪早期，这种对传闻、对法庭上不可采信证据的意识的发展，确实终结了猎巫运动。

sentences.en: So it's got nothing necessarily to do with the belief in witches.
sentences.zh: 所以这不一定与对巫师的信仰有关。

sentences.en: It's really got to do with whether you can translate that belief into action in the courts.
sentences.zh: 这实际上与你是否能将这种信仰转化为法庭上的行动有关。

sentences.en: And then you find, actually, if there are no more witchcraft convictions, then actually some of the heat goes out of it.
sentences.zh: 然后你会发现，实际上，如果没有更多的巫术定罪，那么热度就会消退一些。

sentences.en: Witches just don't seem as, you know, immediate or present because they haven't been convicted.
sentences.zh: 巫师似乎不再那么，你知道，直接或真实存在，因为他们没有被定罪。

sentences.en: Of course, the belief in witches and the belief in the supernatural generally goes on in rural communities in America and in
sentences.zh: 当然，对巫师的信仰和对超自然现象的普遍信仰在美洲和英国的农村社区中一直持续着，

sentences.en: England, you know, beyond the First World War.
sentences.zh: 你知道，甚至在第一次世界大战之后。

sentences.en: And even actually the belief that there are maleficent witches who may be trying to bewitch your cattle or whatever, you know, that persists too, to an extraordinary extent.
sentences.zh: 甚至实际上，认为有邪恶的巫师可能试图对你的牲畜施咒等等，你知道，这种信念也以惊人的程度持续存在。

sentences.en: It's just that sometimes people are lynched.
sentences.zh: 只是有时人们会被私刑处死。

sentences.en: But then, of course, then the lynchers find themselves on the sharp end of the law rather than the witch.
sentences.zh: 但当然，私刑者会发现自己处于法律的严惩之下，而不是巫师。

sentences.en: The witch just becomes a victim of abuse and sometimes sadly murder.
sentences.zh: 巫师只是变成了虐待的受害者，有时悲剧性地变成了谋杀的受害者。

sentences.en: Well, Malcolm, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，马尔科姆，谢谢你。

sentences.en: That was absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这真是太精彩了。

sentences.en: And I think, I mean, I can't recommend
sentences.zh: 而且我想，我的意思是，我极力推荐

sentences.en: The Ruin of All Witches enough.
sentences.zh: 《所有巫师的毁灭》。

sentences.en: And I think the thing that's most moving about it is the way that you give these figures who had such terrible lives, you give them back a kind of dignity.
sentences.zh: 我认为它最感人的地方在于，你赋予了这些生活如此悲惨的人物一种尊严。

sentences.en: You talked about Hugh being a kind of terrible man, but there is, I mean, you know, in the spectacle of his grief for his children, very, very touching, very, very powerful.
sentences.zh: 你谈到休是一个可怕的人，但我的意思是，你知道，在他为孩子悲伤的场景中，非常、非常感人，非常、非常震撼。

sentences.en: So thanks so much for writing it.
sentences.zh: 所以非常感谢你写了这本书。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for coming on the show.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你来到节目中。

sentences.en: And thank you, everyone out there, for listening.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢你们每一位听众。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: It's been great.
sentences.zh: 这很棒。

sentences.en: Cheers.
sentences.zh: 干杯。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余味》。
